q: 1. Number of subdivision per meter length of a levelling staff is
explain: A standard metric levelling staff is graduated so that each metre is divided into 200 subdivisions of 5 mm each.

q: 2. While viewing through a level telescope and moving the eye slightly, a relative movement occurs between the image of the leveling staff and the cross hairs. The instrument is ...............
explain: Parallax occurs when the image formed by the objective does not fall exactly on the plane of the cross-hairs.

q: 3. Diaphragm of a surveying telescope is held inside ...............
options: telescope at the end nearer the eye-piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the cross-hairs is placed in the focal plane of the objective, which is situated just in front of the eye-piece.

q: 4. For the construction of highway (or railway) ...............
options: both longitudinal and cross sections are required
explain: Longitudinal sections are needed for the center-line gradient, and cross-sections are needed to calculate earthwork volumes.

q: 5. Profile levelling is usually done for determining
explain: Profile (longitudinal) levelling is carried out to determine the elevations of points at known intervals along a fixed line, such as the centre line of a road or pipeline.

q: 6. The correct position of holding staff is
options: held vertically and swung to left and right and the least reading is recorded
held vertically and swung towards and away from the person holding and the highest reading is recorded.
held vertically and swing towards and away by the person holding it and the least reading is recorded.
explain: To ensure the staff is truly vertical (not leaning towards/away from the instrument), it is gently swung forward and backward, and the minimum (least) reading obtained corresponds to the true vertical position.

q: 7. An imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level at the centre of the tube is called
explain: The axis of the level tube is a line tangential to the inner surface of the tube at its center point.

q: 8. During levelling generally instrumental error is occuring due to
explain: Collimation error occurs when the line of sight is not truly horizontal even when the bubble is centered, which is a classic instrumental error.

q: 9. In leveling operation
options: the first sight on any change point is a back sight
the second sight on any change point is a fore sight
the line commences with a fore sight and close with a back sight
the line commences with a back sight and closes with a foresight
explain: Every leveling circuit must begin with a Back Sight (on a known Bench Mark) and conclude with a Fore Sight.

q: 10. The sensitivity of the bubble tube can be increased by
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
increasing the diameter of the tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the radius of curvature, the length of the bubble, and the internal diameter of the tube.

q: 11. If temperature increases the sensitivity of a bubble tube
explain: Increased temperature causes the liquid to expand, which decreases the length of the bubble and consequently its sensitivity.

q: 12. In case of leveling staff readings are taken by (In case of target staff)
explain: In target leveling, the instrument man signals the staff man to move the target; once aligned, the staff man reads the value from the staff.

q: 13. Instrumental error in levelling is error due to
explain: All mentioned factors—lack of adjustment, poor bubble response, and loose mechanical parts—are categorized as instrumental errors.

q: 14. Sensitiveness of a level tube depends upon .............
options: the radius of the curvature of its inner surface
the diameter of the level tube
the length of the vapor bubble
explain: Sensitivity increases with a larger radius of curvature, larger diameter, longer bubble length, and lower viscosity/surface tension of the liquid.

q: 15. Permanent adjustment are carried out to
options: establish a fixed relationship between its fundamental axes
explain: Permanent adjustments ensure that the line of collimation, bubble axis, and vertical axis remain in their correct relative geometric positions.

q: 16. The method of levelling used to carry out the reconnaissance of area is
explain: Fly leveling is a rapid method of leveling used to establish approximate elevations or to connect a benchmark to a starting point during reconnaissance.

q: 17. The method of levelling in which the heights of mountains are found by observing the temperature at which water boils is known as
explain: Hypsometry is the method of determining elevation by observing the boiling point of water, which varies with atmospheric pressure (and hence altitude).

q: 18. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called
explain: Differential levelling is the method specifically used to determine the relative heights (difference in elevation) of points on the earth's surface.

q: 19. A line normal to the plumb line at all points is known as
explain: A level line, being everywhere perpendicular to the plumb line (direction of gravity), is a curved line following the level surface of the earth.

q: 20. The sensitivity of the bubble tube expressed in terms of angular value of one division of the bubble is given by
explain: Sensitivity $\alpha = s / (nD)$, where $s$ is the total staff intercept and $D$ is the distance; for one division, it is expressed as $s/D$ radians.

q: 21. The rise and fall method for obtaining the reduced levels of points provides a check in .............
explain: The Rise and Fall method provides a complete check on all readings, including Intermediate Sights.

q: 22. The last reading of levelling is always a
explain: A leveling circuit or run always concludes with a Fore Sight (FS) on a point of known or final elevation.

q: 23. To find the true difference of level between two points, the level should be kept
options: at either of the two points
exactly midway between the two points
at any point on the line joining the two points
explain: To eliminate the effects of curvature, refraction, and collimation error most effectively, the level should ideally be set up exactly midway between the two points being observed.

q: 24. The first reading of leveling is always
explain: Every leveling operation must start with a Back Sight (BS) taken on a point of known elevation (Bench Mark) to establish the Height of Instrument.

q: 25. If the BM of a station A is 500 m. The back sight reading at the point A is 2 m and fore sight reading of station B is 3 m, then find the RL of station B
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL + BS = 500 + 2 = 502 m. RL of B = HI - FS = 502 - 3 = 499 m.

q: 26. In leveling, the effect of refraction may be taken as ............. of that due to curvature.
explain: Refraction correction is generally taken as 1/7th of the curvature correction and is opposite in sign.

q: 27. In levelling, the correction for curvature (in meters) is equal to
explain: The standard formula for the curvature correction, with D in kilometres, is Cc = 0.0785*D2 metres.

q: 28. In levelling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in meters) is equal to
explain: Accounting for the effect of atmospheric refraction (about 1/7th of the curvature effect, in the opposite sense), the combined correction reduces to 0.0673*D2 metres, with D in kilometres.

q: 29. If the level tube is out of adjustment by an angle e, when the telescope is rotated through 180°, it becomes
explain: Rotating the telescope by 180° doubles the angular error relative to the vertical axis, hence 2e.

q: 30. "Cross-sectioning" and "Longitudinal sectioning" is
options: when less number of intermediate sight exist
explain: Profile leveling involves taking readings along a center line (longitudinal) and at right angles to it (cross-sectioning) to map the terrain.

q: 31. The points A and B are 1530 m apart across a wide river... The true difference in level between A and B would be
explain: Using the reciprocal leveling formula: True Difference = [(B1 - A1) + (B2 - A2)] / 2. Based on the table: [(3.810 - 2.165) + (2.355 - 0.91)] / 2 = [1.645 + 1.445] / 2 = 1.545 m.

q: 32. During levelling staff readings are taken 1.0, 0.8 & 0.6 from consecutive horizontal cross hairs, the staff intercept should be
explain: The staff intercept is the difference between the top and bottom hair readings: 1.0 - 0.6 = 0.4.

q: 33. Parallax is an adjustment carried out in
explain: Removal of parallax (by properly focusing the eyepiece and objective) is a key temporary adjustment carried out in levelling instruments before taking readings.

q: 34. Refraction correction .............
options: has no effect on the curvature correction
explain: The refraction correction is negative (subtracts from staff reading) and the curvature correction is positive; since refraction is about 1/7 of curvature, it partially offsets it.

q: 35. The function of levelling head is
options: to attach the theodolite to the tripod
to provide a bearing for the outer hollow spindle
to provide a mean of levelling the instrument
explain: The leveling head serves as the interface between the tripod and the instrument, supporting the vertical axis and housing the leveling mechanism.

q: 36. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction is
explain: Reciprocal leveling involves taking sights from both ends of a line (e.g., across a river) to cancel out errors from earth curvature, atmospheric refraction, and instrument adjustment.

q: 37. Sensitiveness of a level tube is designated by
options: length of bubble of level tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with the radius of curvature of the internal surface of the tube; a larger radius means a more sensitive bubble.

q: 38. A change point is
options: intermediate station where fs and bs taken
station after which instrument is shifted
explain: A change point (CP) is a stable point on which both a Foresight (to close the current setup) and a Backsight (to start the next setup) are taken.

q: 39. Due to curvature of earth the object
explain: The earth's curvature causes a level line to drop away from a horizontal line of sight, making distant objects appear higher than their true elevation relative to the observer.

q: 40. Sensitiveness of bubble tube can be increased by
options: reducing internal radius of the tube
explain: Increasing the diameter or the radius of curvature of the tube allows the bubble to move more significantly for smaller changes in inclination.

q: 41. The angle of field of the telescope .............
options: is independent of the size of the object glass
increases as the size of the eye piece increases
decreases as the distance between eye piece and object increases
explain: The field of view depends primarily on the eyepiece and the magnification, not the size of the objective (object glass), which mainly affects brightness.

q: 42. A staff reading taken on a point whose elevation is to be determined as on a change point is called .............
explain: The last reading taken before moving the instrument is a Foresight.

q: 43. Cross hairs in surveying telescope, are fitted .............
options: at the centre of the telescope
at the optical centre of the eye piece
in front of the eye piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the crosshairs is placed in front of the eyepiece so that they can be focused clearly by the observer.

q: 44. An internal focusing type surveying telescope, may be focused by the movement of .............
explain: In internal focusing telescopes, a double concave lens is moved back and forth between the objective and the diaphragm to focus the image.
